The page is in three parts. The first, **[Time to a picture](#time-to-a-picture)**, times three viewers
— chromosomix, juicebox.js and HiGlass — drawing the same contact map and one track beside it, at the
same resolution, from files on this machine and from the bucket they are published in. The second,
from **[The machine](#the-machine)** on, times the analyses: `{python} R.link('validation')` runs each
analysis twice, through `chromosomix` and through the package it reproduces, and writes every command
it ran to `notebooks/work/validation/commands.json`. This notebook runs each of them again, exactly
as written there but writing to a scratch folder, as a fresh process, `RUNS` times round robin (four,
unless `TIMING_RUNS` in the environment says otherwise), the two sides of each pair taking turns to go
first, and measures what each run costs: its **CPU time**, user and system, of the process and of
every process it started and waited for; its **wall-clock time**; and its **peak memory**, the most
those processes held together: their proportional set sizes — a page two of them share counted half in
each, so that a pool of forked workers is not counted again in every worker — added up four times a
second while the command runs, and never less than the largest resident set any one of them reached,
which a sample can miss. A reference that runs four processes holds what the four hold. Where the
system does not list a process's children, as macOS does not, the peak memory is that largest resident
set alone. The third, **[A deep human map, start to finish](#a-deep-human-map-start-to-finish)**, times
four analyses one after the other over the whole of a human map of a billion contacts, by four
`chromosomix` commands and by one Python script, measured the same way.

Every run of a command is one line of **`notebooks/work/validation/timings.tsv`**, a tidy table — one
row per command and run, one column per variable, the machine and the versions included — every
picture a viewer was timed on is one line of **`viewers.tsv`** beside it, in the same form, and every
step of the pipeline one line of **`pipeline.tsv`**; every table and figure below is drawn from those
three.

**To render.** Render `validation.qmd` first: it fetches the data, makes every input and writes the
command list. The viewers need the app built, the two viewers and a browser for them, and
higlass-python's environment (`notebooks/requirements-higlass.txt`, with libfuse 2 for its URLs).
Then, in the same environment and on a machine left otherwise idle:

```bash
npm run build                                       # the app, served from dist/
npm ci --prefix notebooks/viewers                   # juicebox.js, HiGlass and Playwright, pinned
npx --prefix notebooks/viewers playwright install chromium
python -m venv higlass-env && higlass-env/bin/pip install -r notebooks/requirements-higlass.txt
QUARTO_PYTHON=refs/bin/python quarto render notebooks/timing.qmd
```

The viewers' files (about 15 GB, most of it the mouse map in its two formats) are fetched once into
`notebooks/work/viewers/data/`, and the pipeline's (11.5 GB: the human map, and hg38 for its GC
content) into `notebooks/work/pipeline/data/` — the map linked instead from `laptop.qmd`'s folder, where
that holds it.

A second render reads the tables rather than timing again (`REDO`, `REDO_VIEWERS`, `REDO_PIPELINE`),
unless the command list, the pictures, the number of runs, the pipeline's script or the `chromosomix`
build has changed.
`.github/workflows/notebooks.yml` renders both notebooks on every release, on a fresh GitHub runner
each time, and publishes this page at <https://chromosomix.app/timings/> with the two tables beside
it; the block under the title says which render, and which machine, this is.

```{python}
def show(frame, precision=2, **formats):
    """A table without row numbers: the columns named in `formats` their way, the others to `precision`."""
    return frame.style.hide(axis='index').format(formats or None, precision=precision)


def measures(values):
    """Named numbers as a two-column table."""
    return pd.DataFrame(list(values.items()), columns=['measure', 'value']).style.hide(axis='index')


def machine():
    """What the times were measured on, as columns of the table."""
    cpu = platform.processor()
    if Path('/proc/cpuinfo').exists():
        cpu = next((line.split(':', 1)[1].strip() for line in open('/proc/cpuinfo') if line.startswith('model name')), cpu)
    try:
        memory = round(os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE') * os.sysconf('SC_PHYS_PAGES') / 1e9, 1)
    except (ValueError, OSError):
        memory = np.nan
    node = subprocess.run(['node', '--version'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    return {'processor': cpu, 'cores': os.cpu_count(), 'memory_gb': memory, 'system': platform.platform(),
            'node': node, 'python': platform.python_version()}


MACHINE = machine()
#: Whether the system lists a process's children and its proportional set size, as Linux does: where it does
#: not, as macOS does not, a run's peak memory is that of its largest process alone.
WEIGHS = (Path(f'/proc/self/task/{threading.get_native_id()}/children').exists()
          and Path('/proc/self/smaps_rollup').exists())
#: How often, in seconds, a run's processes are weighed while it runs.
EVERY = 0.25
```

## Time to a picture

How long a reader waits between handing a viewer a contact map with a track and seeing them drawn, in
chromosomix and in the two viewers most used for the same thing:
[juicebox.js](https://github.com/aidenlab/juicebox.js), the browser form of Juicebox, which reads a
`.hic`, and [HiGlass](https://github.com/higlass/higlass), which reads an `.mcool` through a tile server
— here the one higlass-python starts for a file it is given. chromosomix reads both formats and is timed
on each; juicebox.js reads no `.mcool` and HiGlass no `.hic`. Every picture is **one map and one
track**, the same files in every viewer, and it is timed from the moment the viewer is handed them, with
the view, to the moment the viewer itself says the picture is finished:

- **chromosomix**: its own report of a finished picture (`chromosomix:rendered`, SPECS §12), sent once
  every map on screen has been painted from its data, at the resolution the report names, and every
  track beside it drawn;
- **juicebox.js**: no spinner, the map's last repaint covering the state it was asked for, and the
  track holding a tile along each axis, nothing still updating;
- **HiGlass**: every tile of both tracks that is in view fetched and drawn.

**At one resolution, the plan's.** No viewer chooses the resolution. chromosomix is handed a workspace
naming the map at its rung (`map.mcool::/resolutions/25000`); juicebox.js an explicit state, with the
resolution's place in the file's list, the window's first bin and the pixels a bin is drawn at, which
fit the window to its map; HiGlass the window, and the rung as its heatmap's `maxZoom`, its one control
over the resolution, which keeps it from going finer. Each answers with the resolution it drew. A
picture drawn at another resolution, or of part of the window, is kept as what it was, never as a time
for the picture asked for. A view a viewer cannot draw at the plan's resolution is not run, and the
tables say why: a rung the file does not store, or a whole genome, which juicebox.js draws only from the
`.hic`'s own whole-genome matrix, at a resolution of its own.

**From disk and from the bucket.** Each picture is timed from files on this machine and from the same
files where they are published: 4DN's open-data bucket (Amazon S3, us-east-1) for the chicken and the
mouse, the app's demo bucket (eu-west-3) for the yeast. From disk, chromosomix and juicebox.js are given
the files as a reader's drop gives them, and HiGlass's server reads them; before each run from disk the
kernel's page cache is emptied, where the machine lets the benchmark do so (the `page_cache` column), so
that the files are read from the disk, as at a first opening. From the bucket, chromosomix and
juicebox.js read them by range from the page, and HiGlass's server through higlass-python's FUSE mount,
which is how it serves a file it does not hold.

**Nothing carried over.** Every run is a fresh browser context — Chromium, driven by Playwright
(`notebooks/scripts/viewers.mjs`) — with no cache and no storage, and every HiGlass run meets a server
started for it alone, with an empty block cache when it reads from the bucket. The viewer's page is
loaded empty first, with its code and its workers, and that time is kept apart (`app_seconds`): what is
timed is the data's road to the screen. It is then left two seconds, as a reader's page is while they
find their file — what a viewer starts once its page is idle, as chromosomix starts its reader and
h5wasm, a reader finds started — and chromosomix, from disk, as long again on the page its workspace
leaves asking for the files. Each of `VIEWER_RUNS` rounds (four, unless `VIEWER_RUNS` in the environment
says otherwise) draws every picture once, the viewers taking turns to go first, so that the one that
reads a file first, from a disk or from a bucket that answers a second read faster, is a different one
each round. The requests and bytes counted are those the page asked for between the two moments: of the
bucket, for chromosomix and juicebox.js; of its server, for HiGlass, whose own reads go through FUSE,
outside the page, and are not counted.

```{python}
#: Each viewer and the format it is timed on, in the order the tables give them.
VIEWERS = [('chromosomix', 'mcool'), ('chromosomix', 'hic'), ('juicebox', 'hic'), ('higlass', 'mcool')]
LOCATIONS = ['local', 'cloud']
NAMES = {'chromosomix': 'chromosomix', 'juicebox': 'juicebox.js', 'higlass': 'HiGlass'}
WHERE = {'local': 'from disk', 'cloud': 'from the bucket'}


def remote_size(url):
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, method='HEAD')
    with urlopen(request) as response:
        return int(response.headers['Content-Length'])


def fetch_viewer_file(url, md5):
    """A published file, fetched once into work/viewers/data — asked again when its server fails, as
    notebooks/scripts/download.py says — and held to its MD5."""
    path = VDATA / urllib.parse.unquote(url.rsplit('/', 1)[-1])
    if not path.exists():
        print('fetching', url)
        download(url, path)
    digest = hashlib.md5()
    with open(path, 'rb') as handle:
        for block in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 22), b''):
            digest.update(block)
    if digest.hexdigest() != md5:
        raise ValueError(f'{path} is not {url}: its MD5 is {digest.hexdigest()}, not {md5}. '
                         'Delete it, and it is fetched again.')
    return path


VDATA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
WANTED = [GENOMES[g][kind] for g in GENOMES for kind in ('mcool', 'hic', 'track')]
MISSING_BYTES = sum(remote_size(url) for url, _ in WANTED if not (VDATA / url.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]).exists())
FREE_BYTES = shutil.disk_usage(VDATA).free
if MISSING_BYTES > FREE_BYTES - 2e9:
    raise OSError(f'The viewers’ files need {MISSING_BYTES / 1e9:.1f} GB more in {VDATA}, '
                  f'and {FREE_BYTES / 1e9:.1f} GB are free.')
FILES = {g: {kind: {'url': GENOMES[g][kind][0], 'local': fetch_viewer_file(*GENOMES[g][kind])}
             for kind in ('mcool', 'hic', 'track')} for g in GENOMES}
show(pd.DataFrame([{'genome': g, 'data': GENOMES[g]['data'],
                    **{kind: f"{files[kind]['local'].name} ({files[kind]['local'].stat().st_size / 1e9:.2f} GB)"
                       for kind in ('mcool', 'hic', 'track')}} for g, files in FILES.items()]))
```

```{python}
import viewer_plan as vp


def installed(package):
    """A package's version as notebooks/viewers installed it."""
    path = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'viewers' / 'node_modules' / package / 'package.json'
    return json.loads(path.read_text())['version']


def higlass_python():
    """higlass-python's and clodius' versions, in the environment HiGlass's server runs in."""
    probe = 'import importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version("higlass-python"), m.version("clodius"))'
    run = subprocess.run([str(HIGLASS_PYTHON), '-c', probe], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if run.returncode:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'{HIGLASS_PYTHON} cannot run HiGlass’s server: {run.stderr.strip()[-500:]}')
    return run.stdout.split()


def app_build():
    """The build the section times: the app's version, its commit and a fingerprint of the build itself."""
    index = APP_BUILD / 'index.html'
    if not index.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'{index} is not there: build the app first (npm run build).')
    version = json.loads((REPO / 'package.json').read_text())['version']
    commit = subprocess.run(['git', 'rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True, text=True,
                            cwd=REPO).stdout.strip() or 'unknown'
    return f'{version} at {commit}, build {hashlib.sha256(index.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:10]}'


HG_PYTHON, CLODIUS = higlass_python()
VIEWER_VERSION = {'chromosomix': app_build(), 'juicebox': installed('juicebox.js'),
                  'higlass': f"{installed('higlass')}, higlass-python {HG_PYTHON}, clodius {CLODIUS}"}

PLANNED, REFUSED = [], []
for genome, files in FILES.items():
    given = {'mcool': {**files['mcool'], 'info': vp.mcool_info(files['mcool']['local'])},
             'hic': {**files['hic'], 'info': vp.hic_header(files['hic']['local'])},
             'track': {**files['track'], 'names': vp.bigwig_names(files['track']['local'])}}
    runs, refused = vp.runs_for(genome, GENOMES[genome]['views'], given, VIEWERS, LOCATIONS, VWORK)
    PLANNED += runs
    REFUSED += refused

# juicebox's map is narrowed by the track that arrives after it; the driver measures it once, on the yeast.
YEAST_HIC = vp.hic_header(FILES['yeast']['hic']['local'])
PLAN = {
    'app': str(APP_BUILD),
    'higlass': {'python': str(HIGLASS_PYTHON), 'server': str(REPO / 'notebooks' / 'scripts' / 'higlass_server.py')},
    'screenshots': str(VIEWER_SHOTS),
    'limitMs': 300_000,
    'juiceboxProbe': {'map': str(FILES['yeast']['hic']['local']), 'track': str(FILES['yeast']['track']['local']),
                      'chr': [name for name, _ in YEAST_HIC['chromosomes']].index('chrIV'),
                      'zoom': YEAST_HIC['resolutions'].index(3_200)},
    'runs': vp.ordered(PLANNED, VIEWER_RUNS),
}
VIEWER_PLAN.write_text(json.dumps(PLAN, indent=1))
measures({'pictures': len({(run['genome'], run['view'], run['location']) for run in PLANNED}),
          'runs a round, a picture in each viewer that can draw it': len(PLANNED), 'rounds': VIEWER_RUNS,
          'runs in all': len(PLAN['runs']), 'cells refused': len(REFUSED),
          **{NAMES[tool]: version for tool, version in VIEWER_VERSION.items()}})
```

```{python}
#: The columns of viewers.tsv, in order: the picture, the viewer, the run, what it took, where.
VIEWER_COLUMNS = ['genome', 'view', 'window', 'resolution', 'bins', 'viewer', 'format', 'location', 'run', 'status',
                  'seconds', 'app_seconds', 'drawn_resolution', 'drawn_bins', 'requests', 'megabytes', 'note',
                  'page_cache', 'started', 'picture', 'version', *MACHINE, 'chromium', 'map', 'track']


def viewer_rows(results):
    """viewers.tsv: every run of the plan, joined with what the driver measured, and every cell refused."""
    rows = []
    for run in PLAN['runs']:
        got = results.get((run['id'], run['run']), {'status': 'not run', 'note': 'the driver stopped before it'})
        ms, app = got.get('ms'), got.get('appMs')
        rows.append({'genome': run['genome'], 'view': run['view'], 'window': run['window'],
                     'resolution': run['resolution'], 'bins': run['bins'], 'viewer': run['tool'],
                     'format': run['format'], 'location': run['location'], 'run': run['run'],
                     'status': got['status'], 'seconds': None if ms is None else ms / 1000,
                     'app_seconds': None if app is None else app / 1000,
                     'drawn_resolution': got.get('resolution'), 'drawn_bins': got.get('bins'),
                     'requests': got.get('requests'),
                     'megabytes': None if got.get('bytes') is None else got['bytes'] / 1e6,
                     'note': got.get('note') or '', 'page_cache': got.get('page_cache', ''),
                     'started': got.get('started', ''), 'picture': run['picture'],
                     'version': VIEWER_VERSION[run['tool']], **MACHINE, 'chromium': got.get('chromium', ''),
                     'map': Path(run['map']).name, 'track': Path(run['track']).name})
    for cell in REFUSED:
        rows.append({**{key: cell[key] for key in ('genome', 'view', 'window', 'resolution', 'bins', 'format',
                                                     'status', 'note')},
                     'viewer': cell['tool'], 'location': '', 'run': None, 'version': VIEWER_VERSION[cell['tool']],
                     **MACHINE})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=VIEWER_COLUMNS)


def viewers_current():
    """Whether viewers.tsv holds every run of the plan, by these viewers, at these versions."""
    if REDO_VIEWERS or not VIEWER_TABLE.exists():
        return False
    held = pd.read_csv(VIEWER_TABLE, sep='\t')
    timed = held.dropna(subset=['run'])
    wanted = {(run['picture'], run['run']) for run in PLAN['runs']}
    return ({(p, int(r)) for p, r in zip(timed['picture'], timed['run'])} == wanted
            and (timed['status'] != 'not run').all()
            and (held['version'] == held['viewer'].map(VIEWER_VERSION)).all())


if not viewers_current():
    VIEWER_RESULTS.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    shutil.rmtree(VIEWER_SHOTS, ignore_errors=True)
    with open(VWORK / 'driver.log', 'w') as log:
        driver = subprocess.run(['node', str(REPO / 'notebooks' / 'scripts' / 'viewers.mjs'), str(VIEWER_PLAN),
                                 str(VIEWER_RESULTS)], cwd=REPO, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    # A driver that stopped part of the way keeps the runs it finished, and the table says which did not run.
    held = [json.loads(line) for line in VIEWER_RESULTS.read_text().splitlines()] if VIEWER_RESULTS.exists() else []
    VIEWER_TABLE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    viewer_rows({(one['id'], one['run']): one for one in held}).to_csv(VIEWER_TABLE, sep='\t', index=False)
    if driver.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f"The viewers' driver stopped:\n{(VWORK / 'driver.log').read_text()[-3000:]}")
pictures = pd.read_csv(VIEWER_TABLE, sep='\t')
CLIPS = {}
if VIEWER_RESULTS.exists():
    for line in VIEWER_RESULTS.read_text().splitlines():
        one = json.loads(line)
        if one['run'] == 1 and one.get('clip'):
            CLIPS[one['id']] = one['clip']
timed_runs = pictures.dropna(subset=['run'])
#: What a run that drew a picture can say of it; any other run (an error, a time limit) drew none.
PICTURED = ['drawn', 'in part', 'other resolution']
drew = timed_runs[timed_runs['status'].isin(PICTURED)]
measures({'runs in the table': f'{len(timed_runs):,}', 'cells refused': int(pictures['run'].isna().sum()),
          'measured': f"{timed_runs['started'].min()} to {timed_runs['started'].max()}",
          'page cache before a run from disk': ', '.join(sorted(set(timed_runs.loc[timed_runs['location'] == 'local',
                                                                                    'page_cache'].dropna()))),
          'browser': ', '.join(sorted(set(timed_runs['chromium'].dropna()))),
          'table': os.path.relpath(VIEWER_TABLE, REPO)})
```

### What each viewer drew

Median seconds over the runs, from handing the viewer its files to its picture being finished, for each
picture: a genome, a view of it at one resolution, and where the files are read from. A cell that is
not a time says why there is none; a time the viewer did not earn for the picture asked for says what
it drew instead.

```{python}
#| column: page
COLUMN = {(tool, form): f'{NAMES[tool]} · .{form}' for tool, form in VIEWERS}
VIEWS = list(dict.fromkeys(view['view'] for g in GENOMES.values() for view in g['views']))


def cell(rows):
    """One picture in one viewer: the median time, and what it drew if not all of the picture asked for."""
    if rows['run'].isna().all():
        return rows['status'].iloc[0]
    drawn = rows[rows['status'].isin(PICTURED)]
    if drawn.empty:
        return rows['status'].iloc[0]
    text = f"{drawn['seconds'].median():.2f}"
    statuses = set(drawn['status'])
    if 'in part' in statuses:
        text += f" (in part: {drawn.loc[drawn['status'] == 'in part', 'note'].iloc[0]})"
    if 'other resolution' in statuses:
        text += f" (at {int(drawn.loc[drawn['status'] == 'other resolution', 'drawn_resolution'].iloc[0]):,} bp)"
    if len(drawn) < len(rows):
        text += f' ({len(rows) - len(drawn)} of {len(rows)} runs failed)'
    return text


def drawn_table():
    out = []
    for genome in GENOMES:
        for view in GENOMES[genome]['views']:
            for location in LOCATIONS:
                row = {'genome': genome, 'view': view['view'], 'window': view['label'],
                       'resolution (bp)': f"{view['resolution']:,}", 'from': WHERE[location]}
                here = pictures[(pictures['genome'] == genome) & (pictures['view'] == view['view'])]
                for key, name in COLUMN.items():
                    rows = here[(here['viewer'] == key[0]) & (here['format'] == key[1])
                                & ((here['location'] == location) | here['run'].isna())]
                    row[name] = cell(rows) if len(rows) else '—'
                out.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


show(drawn_table())
```

juicebox.js will not draw a chromosome smaller than its map, and it works out how small that is when
the map is loaded, before the track beside it takes some of the map's width: a whole chromosome asked
for is then drawn wider than the map, in part, and that time is not compared below. Every run that drew
something other than the picture asked for, or nothing:

```{python}
#| column: page
def against(other, form):
    """The other viewer's median seconds over chromosomix's on the same file, for each picture both drew whole."""
    out = []
    for (genome, view, location), rows in timed_runs.groupby(['genome', 'view', 'location'], sort=False):
        mine = rows[(rows['viewer'] == 'chromosomix') & (rows['format'] == form)]
        theirs = rows[(rows['viewer'] == other) & (rows['format'] == form)]
        whole = (mine['status'] == 'drawn').all() and (theirs['status'] == 'drawn').all()
        if mine.empty or theirs.empty or not whole:
            continue
        out.append({'genome': genome, 'view': view, 'from': WHERE[location], 'file': f'.{form}',
                    'other viewer': NAMES[other], 'chromosomix s': mine['seconds'].median(),
                    'other s': theirs['seconds'].median()})
    return out
```

## The machine

```{python}
if not MANIFEST.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f'{MANIFEST} is not there: render validation.qmd first.')
LISTED = json.loads(MANIFEST.read_text())
OUT = LISTED['placeholder']
JOBS = [job for job in LISTED['commands'] if job['bench']]
measures({**MACHINE, 'commands timed': f"{len(JOBS)} of the {len(LISTED['commands'])} listed",
          'runs of each': RUNS, 'chromosomix': LISTED['chromosomix'],
          'processes a reference was given, where it takes them': LISTED['threads'],
          'peak memory': (f'every process of a run together, weighed every {EVERY} s' if WEIGHS
                          else 'the largest process of a run alone')})
```

## The runs

Each command is run as `validation.qmd` printed it, from `notebooks/work/validation/`, with its output
sent to a scratch folder that is emptied after the run: all of them once, then all of them again, so a
slow minute of the machine falls on every command rather than on one. `chromosomix` computes on one
thread; a reference that takes a number of processes was given the number in the `threads` column.

**The two sides of a pair take turns to go first.** The list has each analysis's `chromosomix`
commands before its references, and the odd rounds run it so; the even rounds run each analysis's
references first, each side's commands still in their own order. Whichever side runs first reads
from the disk whatever of their shared input the page cache has let go since the round before, and
the side after it finds it in memory. Run in one order, that wait fell on `chromosomix` every time:
a metaplot whose bigWig had gone from the cache spent twelve seconds of its wall clock waiting on
it, and `computeMatrix`, straight after, none. In turns, it falls on each side in half the rounds,
which is why the number of rounds is even.

```{python}
def argv_for(job, scratch):
    """The command as it ran, writing to `scratch`."""
    if job['tool'] == 'chromosomix':
        return job['argv'] + ['--out', os.path.relpath(scratch, WORK)]
    target = os.path.relpath(scratch / job['out'], WORK)
    return [a.replace(OUT, target) for a in job['argv']]


def under(pid):
    """`pid` and every process under it, by the children each of their threads started."""
    found, todo = [], [pid]
    while todo:
        pid = todo.pop()
        found.append(pid)
        try:
            for tid in os.listdir(f'/proc/{pid}/task'):
                with open(f'/proc/{pid}/task/{tid}/children') as handle:
                    todo += [int(child) for child in handle.read().split()]
        except OSError:
            pass
    return found


def pss_kb(pid):
    """A process's proportional set size, in kB: its resident pages, one it shares with others counted as its
    share of it, so that a pool of forked workers is not counted again in each."""
    try:
        with open(f'/proc/{pid}/smaps_rollup') as handle:
            return next(int(line.split()[1]) for line in handle if line.startswith('Pss:'))
    except (OSError, StopIteration):
        return 0


def weigh(pid, done, peak, samples=None):
    """Every EVERY seconds until `done`, the processes under `pid` weighed together, the most into `peak[0]`,
    and each weighing into `samples`, with when it was taken, where there is a list to keep them."""
    while True:
        held = sum(pss_kb(p) for p in under(pid))
        peak[0] = max(peak[0], held)
        if samples is not None:
            samples.append((time.time(), held))
        if done.wait(EVERY):
            return


def timed(argv, extra, cwd=WORK, samples=None):
    """One run, from `cwd` (work/validation/): CPU seconds of the process and every process it started and
    waited for, wall seconds, and the most memory they held together, in MB; every weighing of them into
    `samples`, if it is a list."""
    env = None if extra is None else dict(os.environ, **extra)
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as err:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        process = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=err)
        done, peak = threading.Event(), [0]
        weigher = threading.Thread(target=weigh, args=(process.pid, done, peak, samples), daemon=True)
        if WEIGHS:
            weigher.start()
        _, status, usage = os.wait4(process.pid, 0)
        wall = time.perf_counter() - start
        done.set()
        if WEIGHS:
            weigher.join()
        process.returncode = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
        if process.returncode:
            err.seek(0)
            raise RuntimeError(f'{shlex.join(argv)}\n{err.read().decode(errors="replace")[-3000:]}')
    # ru_maxrss, the largest resident set any one of the processes reached, which a sample can miss: in
    # kilobytes on Linux and in bytes on macOS.
    largest = usage.ru_maxrss / (1024 * 1024 if sys.platform == 'darwin' else 1024)
    return {'cpu_s': usage.ru_utime + usage.ru_stime, 'user_s': usage.ru_utime, 'system_s': usage.ru_stime,
            'wall_s': wall, 'peak_mb': max(peak[0] / 1024, largest)}


#: The columns of the table, in order: what was run, the run, what it cost, where.
COLUMNS = ['section', 'analysis', 'data', 'command', 'tool', 'version', 'variant', 'group', 'threads', 'run',
           'order', 'cpu_s', 'user_s', 'system_s', 'wall_s', 'peak_mb', 'started', *MACHINE, 'chromosomix',
           'command_line']


def round_of(run):
    """The jobs round `run` runs, in its order, each with its place in the list (`order`): as listed on an
    odd round, each analysis's chromosomix commands before its references, and on an even one each
    analysis's references first, each side's commands in their own order."""
    listed = list(enumerate(JOBS))
    if run % 2 == 1:
        return listed
    turned = []
    for _, analysis in groupby(listed, key=lambda pair: (pair[1]['section'], pair[1]['analysis'])):
        analysis = list(analysis)
        turned += [pair for pair in analysis if pair[1]['tool'] != 'chromosomix']
        turned += [pair for pair in analysis if pair[1]['tool'] == 'chromosomix']
    return turned


def benchmark():
    rows = []
    for run in range(1, RUNS + 1):
        for order, job in round_of(run):
            scratch = SCRATCH / job['name']
            shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
            scratch.mkdir(parents=True)
            started = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')
            cost = timed(argv_for(job, scratch), job['env'])
            shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
            rows.append({'section': job['section'], 'analysis': job['analysis'], 'data': job['data'],
                         'command': job['name'], 'tool': job['tool'], 'version': job['version'],
                         'variant': job['variant'], 'group': job['group'], 'threads': job['threads'], 'run': run,
                         'order': order, **cost, 'started': started, **MACHINE,
                         'chromosomix': LISTED['chromosomix'], 'command_line': job['command']})
        # Written after every round, so a long benchmark that is stopped keeps the rounds it finished.
        pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=COLUMNS).to_csv(TIMINGS, sep='\t', index=False)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=COLUMNS)


def current():
    """Whether the table on disk times every command listed, each RUNS times, with the chromosomix listed, in
    this notebook's columns."""
    if REDO or not TIMINGS.exists():
        return False
    held = pd.read_csv(TIMINGS, sep='\t', keep_default_na=False)
    if list(held.columns) != COLUMNS:
        return False
    runs = held.groupby('order')['run'].nunique()
    return (len(runs) == len(JOBS) and set(held['command']) == {job['name'] for job in JOBS}
            and (runs == RUNS).all() and set(held['chromosomix']) == {LISTED['chromosomix']})


if not current():
    SCRATCH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    benchmark()
times = pd.read_csv(TIMINGS, sep='\t', keep_default_na=False)
measures({'runs in the table': f'{len(times):,}', 'columns': len(times.columns),
          'measured': f"{times['started'].min()} to {times['started'].max()}", 'table': os.path.relpath(TIMINGS, REPO)})
```

```{python}
       .agg(cpu=('cpu_s', 'mean'), cpu_sd=('cpu_s', 'std'), wall=('wall_s', 'mean'), wall_sd=('wall_s', 'std'),
            peak=('peak_mb', 'max'))
       .reset_index().sort_values('order').reset_index(drop=True))
```

## Against the references

For each analysis, the `chromosomix` commands against the reference commands they are paired with — the
same variant, or the analysis's one reference — as a fold: the reference's seconds over the app's,
summed where a side is several commands, which the table names. deepTools' metaplot is
`computeMatrix` and then `plotProfile` — and `plotHeatmap`, over two tracks — against one
`chromosomix metaplot`; its track correlation is `multiBigwigSummary` and then `plotCorrelation` once
a method, against `chromosomix trackcorr` once a method.

```{python}
#| column: page
#: Each timed command's line, by its name, for what the pairs below add up.
LINES = {job['name']: job['command'] for job in JOBS}


def program(name):
    """What a timed command runs: chromosomix's task, a reference script's name, or the program."""
    words = shlex.split(LINES[name])
    if words[0] == 'chromosomix':
        return words[1]
    if words[0].endswith('python'):
        return Path(words[1]).stem
    return words[0]


def summed(rows):
    """The commands one side of a pair adds up, in order, a repeated one counted: `plotCorrelation ×2`."""
    counts = Counter(program(name) for name in rows['command'])
    return ' + '.join(name if n == 1 else f'{name} ×{n}' for name, n in counts.items())


def pairs():
    out = []
    for (section, analysis), rows in per.groupby(['section', 'analysis'], sort=False):
        apps, refs = rows[rows['tool'] == 'chromosomix'], rows[rows['tool'] != 'chromosomix']
        for group, mine in apps.groupby('group', sort=False):
            theirs = refs[refs['group'] == group]
            if theirs.empty and refs['group'].nunique() == 1:
                theirs = refs
            if theirs.empty:
                continue
            out.append({'section': section, 'analysis': analysis, 'variant': group or '—',
                        'reference': ', '.join(dict.fromkeys(theirs['tool'])),
                        'chromosomix commands': summed(mine), 'reference commands': summed(theirs),
                        'chromosomix CPU s': mine['cpu'].sum(), 'reference CPU s': theirs['cpu'].sum(),
                        'chromosomix wall s': mine['wall'].sum(), 'reference wall s': theirs['wall'].sum(),
                        'chromosomix peak MB': mine['peak'].max(), 'reference peak MB': theirs['peak'].max()})
    frame = pd.DataFrame(out)
    frame['× faster, CPU'] = frame['reference CPU s'] / frame['chromosomix CPU s']
    frame['× faster, wall'] = frame['reference wall s'] / frame['chromosomix wall s']
    return frame


folds = pairs()
show(folds, **{'× faster, CPU': '{:.1f}×', '× faster, wall': '{:.1f}×', 'chromosomix peak MB': '{:,.0f}',
               'reference peak MB': '{:,.0f}'})
```

```{python}
fold = folds['× faster, CPU']
TEXT = {'fold': f'{np.exp(np.log(fold).mean()):.1f}', 'n': f'{len(fold)}',
        'range': f'{fold.min():.1f}× to {fold.max():.1f}×',
        'slower': ', '.join(f"{a} ({v})" for a, v, f in zip(folds['analysis'], folds['variant'], fold) if f < 1) or 'none',
        'sd': f"{(per['cpu_sd'] / per['cpu']).max():.0%}",
        'wall': f"{np.exp(np.log(folds['× faster, wall']).mean()):.1f}"}
```

Over the `{python} TEXT['n']` pairs, `chromosomix` takes **`{python} TEXT['fold']` times less CPU** than
the reference tools, as a geometric mean of the folds above (`{python} TEXT['range']`), and
`{python} TEXT['wall']` times less wall-clock time. Slower than its reference: `{python} TEXT['slower']`.
No command's CPU time spreads by more than `{python} TEXT['sd']` of its mean across runs.

```{python}
#| label: fig-time
#| fig-cap: "CPU time of every job, one row a side of a pair in the table above, its commands added up run by run (deepTools' computeMatrix and plotProfile on one line); each run a dot and the mean a bar, on a logarithmic axis; the rows of one analysis share a band."
def jobs():
    """One row a side of each pair: an analysis's chromosomix commands of one group, or its reference's, with
    every run's CPU seconds added up across them, as the pairs above add them."""
    side = np.where(per['tool'] == 'chromosomix', 'chromosomix', 'reference')
    out = []
    for (section, analysis, _, group), rows in per.groupby(['section', 'analysis', side, 'group'], sort=False):
        # By their places in the list: an analysis may give its chromosomix command and its reference one name.
        runs_ = times[times['order'].isin(rows['order'])].groupby('run')['cpu_s'].sum()
        groups = per.loc[(per['section'] == section) & (per['analysis'] == analysis), 'group'].nunique()
        if len(rows) == 1:
            what = rows['variant'].iloc[0]
        else:
            what = (f'{group}: ' if groups > 1 and group else '') + summed(rows)
        out.append({'section': section, 'analysis': analysis, 'tool': ', '.join(dict.fromkeys(rows['tool'])),
                    'what': what, 'runs': runs_.to_numpy(), 'cpu': runs_.mean()})
    return out


JOB_ROWS = jobs()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 0.36 * len(JOB_ROWS) + 1.2), layout='constrained')
y = np.arange(len(JOB_ROWS))[::-1]
BANDS = [row['analysis'] for row in JOB_ROWS]
for k, analysis in enumerate(dict.fromkeys(BANDS)):
    if k % 2:
        at = y[[i for i, one in enumerate(BANDS) if one == analysis]]
        ax.axhspan(at.min() - 0.5, at.max() + 0.5, color=MISSING, lw=0, zorder=0)
for yi, row in zip(y, JOB_ROWS):
    colour = APP_COLOUR if row['tool'] == 'chromosomix' else REF
    ax.scatter(row['runs'], np.full(len(row['runs']), yi), s=14, color=colour, alpha=0.55, lw=0, zorder=3)
    ax.plot([row['cpu']] * 2, [yi - 0.3, yi + 0.3], color=colour, lw=2.5, zorder=4)
labels = [f"{row['section']} · {row['analysis']} · {row['tool']}" + (f" ({row['what']})" if row['what'] else '')
          for row in JOB_ROWS]
ax.set_yticks(y, labels, fontsize=8)
ax.set_xscale('log')
# Not EVERY, the weighing's interval, which the pipeline's runs below read again.
ALL_RUNS = np.concatenate([row['runs'] for row in JOB_ROWS])
ax.set_xlim(ALL_RUNS.min() / 1.5, ALL_RUNS.max() * 1.5)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f'{v:g}'))
ax.xaxis.set_minor_locator(NullLocator())
ax.set(xlabel='CPU time (s)', ylim=(-0.5, len(JOB_ROWS) - 0.5))
ax.grid(axis='y', visible=False)
ax.scatter([], [], s=24, color=APP_COLOUR, label='chromosomix')
ax.scatter([], [], s=24, color=REF, label='reference')
ax.legend(loc='upper right')
plt.show()
```

```{python}
y = np.arange(len(folds))[::-1]
ax.scatter(folds['× faster, CPU'], y, s=36, color=APP_COLOUR, label='CPU', zorder=3)
ax.scatter(folds['× faster, wall'], y, s=36, facecolors='none', edgecolors=APP_COLOUR, label='wall clock', zorder=3)
```

## A deep human map, start to finish

Each command above is one analysis, timed alone, on a map of at most 69 million contacts. This last
part times what a reader runs on a deep map: four analyses, one after the other, over the whole genome
of 4DN's in situ Hi-C of IMR-90 (Rao et al. 2014; 4DNFIJTOIGOI, GRCh38, 1.08 billion contacts, an
8.3 GB `.mcool`), each with the settings its section of the validation holds it to:

1. **Loop calling** at 10 kb: HiCCUPS as `cooltools.dots` computes it, at its Python API's defaults,
   over the expected with the first two diagonals left out (§ 19);
2. **Diamond insulation** at 10 kb, a window of 10 bins, 100 kb, and its boundaries (§ 1);
3. **Compartments** at 250 kb: three cis eigenvectors, signed by each bin's GC content, which is
   worked out once beforehand — `bioframe.frac_gc` over hg38 as Illumina iGenomes distributes UCSC's —
   and given to both (§ 3);
4. **APA over every loop** step 1 called: five bins either side of each, ±50 kb, every window over the
   expected, the first two diagonals left out and no loop for being near the diagonal (§ 11, *over the
   expected, every loop*).

**chromosomix** runs them as a shell script would: four commands, one after the other, the last
reading the loops the first wrote. **The reference** is one Python script,
`notebooks/scripts/cooltools_pipeline.py`, which runs the four through cooltools and coolpuppy in one
process, its pileup over the loops `cooltools.dots` called and the expected computed for them. So the
script pays for its pileup's expected in loop calling, where `chromosomix apa` computes its own, along
the diagonals its windows reach; and chromosomix's compartments draw the saddle too, at the task's
default, which `cooltools.eigs_cis` does not. `chromosomix` computes on one thread; the script gives
every call that takes them as many processes as every reference above was given (the `threads`
column).

**Start-up, each step and the whole.** A command's start-up is the program loaded and nothing done,
`chromosomix --version`, timed as a command of its own, which each of the four pays again before its
task: each step is its command, from its launch to its exit, its own start-up and the opening of the
map included, and the whole is the four. The script's start-up runs from its launch to the end of its
imports — Python itself, cooler, cooltools and coolpuppy — and each step from the end of the one before
it to its own, as the script writes them down; the whole is the process, from its launch to its exit.
CPU time and memory are measured as for every command above: a command's, and the script's whole, by
`os.wait4` and by weighing its processes every `EVERY` seconds; a step of the script's, by the CPU its
process and every child it had waited for had used at either end — cooltools' and coolpuppy's pools are
waited for when each call returns — and by the most its processes held together in the weighings taken
between them.

**One run of each side, unless `PIPELINE_RUNS` says otherwise.** Each side reads the map from the disk,
the page cache emptied before it where the machine lets the benchmark do so; where it does not, the map
is read through once before each side instead, so that both find it in memory (the `page_cache`
column). Over several runs the two take turns to go first. Every step of every run, its start-up and the
whole among them, is one line of **`notebooks/work/validation/pipeline.tsv`**, published beside
`timings.tsv`.

```{python}
import cooler

PIPELINE_DATA = PWORK / 'data'
#: The map, and the sequence its compartments are signed by: where each is published, and its MD5.
PIPELINE_FILES = {
    '4DNFIJTOIGOI.mcool': (f'{FOURDN_FILES}/b4939d95-4121-4f86-9cc8-29a34eb834ef/4DNFIJTOIGOI.mcool',
                           '659f9dc7613650494aa5ed4138e2e17e'),
    'hg38.fa': ('https://ngi-igenomes.s3.amazonaws.com/igenomes/Homo_sapiens/UCSC/hg38/Sequence/WholeGenomeFasta/'
                'genome.fa', '9ce261c4aaf4b6092888ef298d190da2'),
}
#: Where laptop.qmd keeps the same map, which is linked from there rather than fetched again.
LAPTOP_DATA = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'work' / 'laptop' / 'data'


def md5_of(path):
    digest = hashlib.md5()
    with open(path, 'rb') as handle:
        for block in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 22), b''):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def pipeline_file(name, url, md5):
    """A published file, in work/pipeline/data — linked from the laptop's folder where that holds it, and
    otherwise fetched once, asked again when its server fails — and held to its MD5."""
    path = PIPELINE_DATA / name
    if not path.exists() and (LAPTOP_DATA / name).exists():
        path.symlink_to((LAPTOP_DATA / name).resolve())
    if not path.exists():
        print('fetching', url)
        download(url, path)
    if md5_of(path) != md5:
        raise ValueError(f'{path} is not {url}: its MD5 is not {md5}. Delete it, and it is fetched again.')
    return path


PIPELINE_DATA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
P_MISSING = sum(remote_size(url) for name, (url, _) in PIPELINE_FILES.items()
                if not (PIPELINE_DATA / name).exists() and not (LAPTOP_DATA / name).exists())
P_FREE = shutil.disk_usage(PIPELINE_DATA).free
if P_MISSING > P_FREE - 2e9:
    raise OSError(f'The pipeline’s files need {P_MISSING / 1e9:.1f} GB more in {PIPELINE_DATA}, '
                  f'and {P_FREE / 1e9:.1f} GB are free.')
IMR90, HG38 = (pipeline_file(name, *where) for name, where in PIPELINE_FILES.items())

# The GC content of each 250-kb bin of the map, once: a table for cooltools, a bedGraph for chromosomix.
GC_TSV, GC_BEDGRAPH = PWORK / 'gc-250kb.tsv', PWORK / 'gc-250kb.bedGraph'
if REDO_PIPELINE or not GC_TSV.exists():
    import bioframe
    import pyfaidx

    pyfaidx.Faidx(str(HG38)).close()
    _bins = cooler.Cooler(f'{IMR90}::/resolutions/250000').bins()[['chrom', 'start', 'end']][:]
    _gc = bioframe.frac_gc(_bins, bioframe.load_fasta(str(HG38), engine='pyfaidx'))
    _gc.to_csv(GC_TSV, sep='\t', index=False)
    _gc.dropna()[['chrom', 'start', 'end', 'GC']].to_csv(GC_BEDGRAPH, sep='\t', header=False, index=False)
_c10 = cooler.Cooler(f'{IMR90}::/resolutions/10000')
_gc_bins = pd.read_csv(GC_TSV, sep='\t')
measures({'map': f"{IMR90.name} ({IMR90.stat().st_size / 1e9:.1f} GB): {len(_c10.chromnames)} sequences, "
                 f"{_c10.info['sum']:,} contacts",
          'at 10 kb': f"{_c10.info['nbins']:,} bins, {_c10.info['nnz']:,} pixels",
          'at 250 kb, GC content': f"{len(_gc_bins):,} bins, {int(_gc_bins['GC'].notna().sum()):,} with sequence",
          'sequence': f'{HG38.name} ({HG38.stat().st_size / 1e9:.1f} GB)'})
```

The commands, from `notebooks/work/pipeline/`, as the first run wrote them; each run writes into a
folder of its own side, emptied before it:

```{python}
from importlib.metadata import version as installed_version

CLI = REPO / 'dist-cli' / 'chromosomix.mjs'
PIPELINE_SCRIPT = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'scripts' / 'cooltools_pipeline.py'
#: The four steps, in their order: what the tables call each, and what it reads.
PIPELINE_STEPS = {'loops': ('Loop calling', '10 kb'), 'insulation': ('Diamond insulation', '10 kb, 10 bins'),
                  'compartments': ('Compartments', '250 kb, GC-phased'),
                  'apa': ('APA over every loop', '10 kb, ±5 bins, over the expected')}
#: And the start-up before them, and the whole of them.
PIPELINE_TASKS = {'start-up': ('Start-up', ''), **PIPELINE_STEPS, 'total': ('Total', '')}
P_THREADS = LISTED['threads']
P_SIDES = {'chromosomix': 'chromosomix',
           'reference': ', '.join(f'{name} {installed_version(name)}' for name in ('cooltools', 'coolpuppy', 'cooler'))}
P_SCRIPT = hashlib.sha256(PIPELINE_SCRIPT.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:10]
P_OUT = {side: PWORK / 'runs' / side for side in P_SIDES}


def p_rel(path):
    return os.path.relpath(path, PWORK)


def p_map(bp):
    return f'{p_rel(IMR90)}::/resolutions/{bp}'


def app_argv(step, out):
    """chromosomix's command for one step, writing into `out`: the pileup reads the loops the first wrote there."""
    program = ['node', p_rel(CLI)]
    if step == 'start-up':
        return [*program, '--version']
    argv = {'loops': ['loops', p_map(10_000)],
            'insulation': ['insulation', p_map(10_000), '--window', '10'],
            'compartments': ['compartments', p_map(250_000), '--components', '3', '--phaseTrack', p_rel(GC_BEDGRAPH)]}
    if step == 'apa':
        argv['apa'] = ['apa', p_map(10_000), '--pairs', p_rel(one_file(out / 'loops', '*.loops-calls.bedpe')),
                       '--mode', 'fixed', '--window', '5', '--minDiag', '2', '--minDist', '0', '--norm', 'oe']
    return [*program, *argv[step], '--out', p_rel(out / step)]


def script_argv(out):
    """The script's one command, writing beside `out/cooltools` and its marks to `out/marks.json`."""
    return [sys.executable, p_rel(PIPELINE_SCRIPT), p_rel(IMR90), p_rel(GC_TSV), p_rel(out / 'cooltools'),
            str(P_THREADS), p_rel(out / 'marks.json')]


def one_file(folder, pattern):
    hits = sorted(Path(folder).glob(pattern))
    if len(hits) != 1:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'{len(hits)} files match {pattern} in {folder}')
    return hits[0]


def typed_line(argv):
    """A command as a reader would type it."""
    if argv[:2] == ['node', p_rel(CLI)]:
        argv = ['chromosomix', *argv[2:]]
    return shlex.join(['python' if a == sys.executable else a for a in argv])


def settle():
    """Before each side: the page cache emptied where the machine lets the benchmark do so, so that each reads
    the map from the disk, as at a first opening; elsewhere the map read through once, so that each finds it
    in memory. Which of the two, as the table says it."""
    subprocess.run(['sync'])
    try:
        if subprocess.run(['sudo', '-n', 'sh', '-c', 'echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'],
                          capture_output=True).returncode == 0:
            return 'dropped'
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    with open(IMR90, 'rb') as handle:
        while handle.read(1 << 24):
            pass
    return 'read through'


#: The columns of pipeline.tsv, in order: the side and the step, the run, what it cost, where.
PIPELINE_COLUMNS = ['side', 'tool', 'version', 'step', 'task', 'reads', 'run', 'went_first', 'page_cache',
                    'threads', 'cpu_s', 'wall_s', 'peak_mb', 'started', *MACHINE, 'chromosomix', 'script', 'map',
                    'command_line']


def p_row(side, step, run, first, cache, cost, line, started):
    return {'side': side, 'tool': 'chromosomix' if side == 'chromosomix' else 'cooltools, coolpuppy',
            'version': LISTED['chromosomix'] if side == 'chromosomix' else P_SIDES[side], 'step': step,
            'task': PIPELINE_TASKS[step][0], 'reads': PIPELINE_TASKS[step][1], 'run': run,
            'went_first': first == side, 'page_cache': cache,
            'threads': 1 if side == 'chromosomix' else P_THREADS, 'cpu_s': cost['cpu_s'], 'wall_s': cost['wall_s'],
            'peak_mb': cost['peak_mb'], 'started': started, **MACHINE, 'chromosomix': LISTED['chromosomix'],
            'script': P_SCRIPT, 'map': IMR90.name, 'command_line': line}


def app_side(run, first):
    """chromosomix's side of one run: its start-up, its four commands and their whole."""
    out = P_OUT['chromosomix']
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    cache, rows = settle(), []
    for step in ['start-up', *PIPELINE_STEPS]:
        argv = app_argv(step, out)
        started = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')
        rows.append(p_row('chromosomix', step, run, first, cache, timed(argv, None, cwd=PWORK), typed_line(argv),
                          started))
    steps = rows[1:]
    whole = {'cpu_s': sum(r['cpu_s'] for r in steps), 'wall_s': sum(r['wall_s'] for r in steps),
             'peak_mb': max(r['peak_mb'] for r in steps)}
    rows.append(p_row('chromosomix', 'total', run, first, cache, whole,
                      '; '.join(r['command_line'] for r in steps), steps[0]['started']))
    return rows


def script_side(run, first):
    """The script's side of one run: its start-up and four steps as it marked them, and its whole."""
    out = P_OUT['reference']
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    cache, samples = settle(), []
    argv = script_argv(out)
    started = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')
    launched = time.time()
    whole = timed(argv, None, cwd=PWORK, samples=samples)
    marks = {mark['step']: mark for mark in json.loads((out / 'marks.json').read_text())['marks']}
    rows, before = [], {'time': launched, 'cpu_s': 0.0}
    for step, mark in [('start-up', marks['imported']), *((step, marks[step]) for step in PIPELINE_STEPS)]:
        held = [kb for at, kb in samples if before['time'] <= at <= mark['time']]
        cost = {'cpu_s': mark['cpu_s'] - before['cpu_s'], 'wall_s': mark['time'] - before['time'],
                'peak_mb': max(held) / 1024 if held else np.nan}
        rows.append(p_row('reference', step, run, first, cache, cost, typed_line(argv), started))
        before = mark
    rows.append(p_row('reference', 'total', run, first, cache, whole, typed_line(argv), started))
    return rows


def pipeline():
    rows = []
    PIPELINE_TABLE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for run in range(1, PIPELINE_RUNS + 1):
        # chromosomix first on odd runs, the script on even ones.
        order = ['chromosomix', 'reference'] if run % 2 == 1 else ['reference', 'chromosomix']
        for side in order:
            rows += app_side(run, order[0]) if side == 'chromosomix' else script_side(run, order[0])
        # Written after every run, so a long benchmark that is stopped keeps the runs it finished.
        pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=PIPELINE_COLUMNS).to_csv(PIPELINE_TABLE, sep='\t', index=False)


def pipeline_current():
    """Whether pipeline.tsv holds every step of PIPELINE_RUNS runs, by this chromosomix and this script."""
    if REDO_PIPELINE or not PIPELINE_TABLE.exists():
        return False
    held = pd.read_csv(PIPELINE_TABLE, sep='\t', keep_default_na=False)
    return (list(held.columns) == PIPELINE_COLUMNS and set(held['run']) == set(range(1, PIPELINE_RUNS + 1))
            and len(held) == PIPELINE_RUNS * 2 * len(PIPELINE_TASKS)
            and set(held['chromosomix']) == {LISTED['chromosomix']} and set(held['script']) == {P_SCRIPT}
            and all(P_OUT[side].exists() for side in P_SIDES))


if not pipeline_current():
    pipeline()
steps = pd.read_csv(PIPELINE_TABLE, sep='\t', keep_default_na=False, na_values=[''])
for side, rows in steps.groupby('side', sort=False):
    print(f'# {rows["tool"].iloc[0]}')
    lines = rows.loc[(rows['run'] == 1) & ~rows['step'].isin(['total']), 'command_line']
    print('\n'.join(f'$ {line}' for line in dict.fromkeys(lines)), end='\n\n')
measures({'runs': PIPELINE_RUNS, 'lines in the table': len(steps),
          'measured': f"{steps['started'].min()} to {steps['started'].max()}",
          'page cache before each side': ', '.join(sorted(set(steps['page_cache']))),
          'reference': P_SIDES['reference'], 'table': os.path.relpath(PIPELINE_TABLE, REPO)})
```

CPU and wall-clock seconds and peak memory, mean over the runs, for each side's start-up, each step
and the whole:

```{python}
#| column: page
P_SIDE_NAMES = {'chromosomix': 'chromosomix', 'reference': 'cooltools, coolpuppy'}
p_mean = (steps.groupby(['step', 'side'], sort=False)
          .agg(cpu=('cpu_s', 'mean'), wall=('wall_s', 'mean'), peak=('peak_mb', 'max')).reset_index())
p_table = p_mean.pivot(index='step', columns='side', values=['cpu', 'wall', 'peak']).reindex(list(PIPELINE_TASKS))
p_shown = pd.DataFrame({'step': [PIPELINE_TASKS[s][0] for s in p_table.index],
                        'reads': [PIPELINE_TASKS[s][1] for s in p_table.index]})
for measure, unit in (('cpu', 'CPU s'), ('wall', 'wall s'), ('peak', 'peak MB')):
    for side in P_SIDES:
        p_shown[f'{P_SIDE_NAMES[side]}, {unit}'] = p_table[(measure, side)].to_numpy()
p_shown['× faster, wall'] = p_table[('wall', 'reference')].to_numpy() / p_table[('wall', 'chromosomix')].to_numpy()
show(p_shown, **{column: '{:,.0f}' for column in p_shown.columns if column.endswith('MB')},
     **{'× faster, wall': '{:.1f}×'})
```

Both sides did the same work: what each wrote in the last run, step by step, against the other's.

```{python}
APP_P, REF_P = P_OUT['chromosomix'], P_OUT['reference']


def app_table(folder, pattern):
    return pd.read_csv(one_file(folder, pattern), sep='\t', comment='#')


p_agree = []
# Loop calling: the same bin pairs.
_app_dots = app_table(APP_P / 'loops', '*.loops-table.tsv')
_ref_dots = pd.read_csv(REF_P / 'cooltools-loops.tsv', sep='\t').rename(columns={'chrom1': 'sequence'})
_dots = _app_dots.merge(_ref_dots, on=['sequence', 'start1', 'start2'], how='outer', indicator=True)
p_agree.append({'step': 'Loop calling', 'chromosomix': f'{len(_app_dots):,} loops',
                'cooltools, coolpuppy': f'{len(_ref_dots):,} loops',
                'agreement': f"{int((_dots['_merge'] == 'both').sum()):,} at the same bin pair, "
                             f"{int((_dots['_merge'] != 'both').sum()):,} in one only"})
# Insulation: every bin both score, and the boundaries.
_app_ins = app_table(APP_P / 'insulation', '*.insulation-w10.tsv')['value'].to_numpy(float)
_ref_table = pd.read_csv(REF_P / 'cooltools-insulation.tsv', sep='\t')
_ref_ins = _ref_table['log2_insulation_score_100000'].to_numpy(float)
_both = np.isfinite(_app_ins) & np.isfinite(_ref_ins)
_app_b = app_table(APP_P / 'insulation', '*.insulation-boundaries.tsv')
_ref_b = _ref_table.loc[_ref_table['is_boundary_100000'].astype(bool), ['chrom', 'start']]
_same_b = len(_app_b[['chrom', 'start']].merge(_ref_b, on=['chrom', 'start']))
p_agree.append({'step': 'Diamond insulation', 'chromosomix': f'{len(_app_b):,} boundaries',
                'cooltools, coolpuppy': f'{len(_ref_b):,} boundaries',
                'agreement': f'{_same_b:,} boundaries at the same bin; over {_both.sum():,} bins, the score '
                             f'within {np.abs(_app_ins[_both] - _ref_ins[_both]).max():.1e}'})
# Compartments: E1, chromosome by chromosome, chrY left out as § 3 leaves it out.
_app_e1 = app_table(APP_P / 'compartments', '*.compartment-e1.tsv')['value'].to_numpy(float)
_ref_vec = pd.read_csv(REF_P / 'cooltools-eigenvectors.tsv', sep='\t')
_rs = {}
for _chrom in _ref_vec['chrom'].unique():
    _s = (_ref_vec['chrom'] == _chrom).to_numpy()
    _ok = _s & np.isfinite(_app_e1) & np.isfinite(_ref_vec['E1'].to_numpy(float))
    if _chrom != 'chrY' and _ok.sum() > 2:
        _rs[_chrom] = np.corrcoef(_app_e1[_ok], _ref_vec['E1'].to_numpy(float)[_ok])[0, 1]
_low = min(_rs, key=_rs.get)
p_agree.append({'step': 'Compartments', 'chromosomix': 'E1, E2, E3', 'cooltools, coolpuppy': 'E1, E2, E3',
                'agreement': f'E1 at 1 − r ≤ {max(1 - _rs[_low], 1e-16):.0e} (Pearson) on each of {len(_rs)} '
                             f'chromosomes, {_low} the furthest'})
# The pileup: cell for cell.
_app_apa = app_table(APP_P / 'apa', '*.apa-0.tsv')
_app_apa = _app_apa.set_index(_app_apa.columns[0]).to_numpy(float)
_ref_apa = np.loadtxt(REF_P / 'cooltools-apa.tsv', delimiter='\t')
_cells = np.isfinite(_app_apa) & np.isfinite(_ref_apa)
_rel = np.abs(_app_apa - _ref_apa)[_cells] / np.maximum(np.abs(_ref_apa[_cells]), 1e-300)
p_agree.append({'step': 'APA over every loop', 'chromosomix': f'{_app_apa.shape[0]} × {_app_apa.shape[1]}',
                'cooltools, coolpuppy': f'{_ref_apa.shape[0]} × {_ref_apa.shape[1]}',
                'agreement': f'{_cells.sum()} cells, within {_rel.max():.1e} of each other, relative; '
                             f'{int((np.isfinite(_app_apa) != np.isfinite(_ref_apa)).sum())} empty in one only'})
show(pd.DataFrame(p_agree))
```

```{python}
def p_value(step, side, column):
    return float(steps.loc[(steps['step'] == step) & (steps['side'] == side), column].mean())


def minutes(seconds):
    return f'{seconds / 60:.1f} min' if seconds >= 90 else f'{seconds:.0f} s'


P_TEXT = {'app': minutes(p_value('total', 'chromosomix', 'wall_s')),
          'ref': minutes(p_value('total', 'reference', 'wall_s')),
          'wall': f"{p_value('total', 'reference', 'wall_s') / p_value('total', 'chromosomix', 'wall_s'):.1f}",
          'cpu': f"{p_value('total', 'reference', 'cpu_s') / p_value('total', 'chromosomix', 'cpu_s'):.1f}",
          'app_peak': f"{steps.loc[steps['side'] == 'chromosomix', 'peak_mb'].max() / 1024:.1f} GB",
          'ref_peak': f"{steps.loc[steps['side'] == 'reference', 'peak_mb'].max() / 1024:.1f} GB",
          'app_start': f"{p_value('start-up', 'chromosomix', 'wall_s'):.2f} s",
          'ref_start': f"{p_value('start-up', 'reference', 'wall_s'):.1f} s",
          'loops': f"{p_value('loops', 'reference', 'wall_s') / p_value('loops', 'chromosomix', 'wall_s'):.1f}"}


def against(step):
    """A step of chromosomix's against the script's: × on the wall clock and × in CPU time, above 1 faster."""
    name = PIPELINE_TASKS[step][0]
    return (f"{name if name[:3].isupper() else name.lower()}, "
            f"{p_value(step, 'reference', 'wall_s') / p_value(step, 'chromosomix', 'wall_s'):.1f}× on the wall clock "
            f"and {p_value(step, 'reference', 'cpu_s') / p_value(step, 'chromosomix', 'cpu_s'):.1f}× in CPU time")


P_SLOWER = [step for step in PIPELINE_STEPS if p_value(step, 'chromosomix', 'wall_s') > p_value(step, 'reference', 'wall_s')]
P_TEXT['slower'] = ('In none of the four is chromosomix slower on the wall clock.' if not P_SLOWER else
                    'On one thread against the script\'s processes, chromosomix is slower on the wall clock at '
                    + '; '.join(against(step) for step in P_SLOWER) + '.')
```

Over the whole IMR-90 map, the four analyses take **`{python} P_TEXT['app']`** in `chromosomix` and
**`{python} P_TEXT['ref']`** in the Python script: `{python} P_TEXT['wall']` times less wall-clock time
on one thread against the script's `{python} str(P_THREADS)` processes, and `{python} P_TEXT['cpu']` times less CPU
time; at most `{python} P_TEXT['app_peak']` of memory against `{python} P_TEXT['ref_peak']`. Loop
calling is most of either side, and `{python} P_TEXT['loops']` times faster on the wall clock in
`chromosomix`. `{python} P_TEXT['slower']` Starting takes `chromosomix` `{python} P_TEXT['app_start']`
a command, four times, and the script `{python} P_TEXT['ref_start']`, once.
